title: How to dictate an email in Apple Mail on Mac: step by step, with fixes

description: Learn how to dictate an email in Apple Mail on Mac with Dictation, the Edit menu, punctuation commands, and fixes when Start Dictation is missing.

intro: Turn on Dictation under System Settings > Keyboard, then click in the message body and choose Edit > Start Dictation. Speak your email, say "new paragraph" for a blank line, and press Escape when you finish.

blocks.text: What dictation in Apple Mail actually is

Apple Mail has no dictation feature of its own. Apple's Mail User Guide has no section on dictation or voice input for writing messages. What you use is macOS Dictation, the system-wide voice input that works in text fields across your Mac. Mail gives you the place to put the text.

That sounds like a limitation, but it works in your favor. Once you learn Dictation in Mail, the same steps work in most other apps where you can type. Mail adds one small detail. You must click in the message body first, because Dictation needs a cursor to write into.

A 2022 Apple Community thread shows the same problem. A user could not find a microphone icon in Mail. The top answer was to click into the message body and choose Edit > Start Dictation, after which the icon appeared. That thread does not name a macOS version, so treat it as a pattern, not a guarantee.
Turn on Dictation on Mac before you start

Dictation has to be on before Mail can use it. Open the Apple menu, choose System Settings, then click Keyboard and select Dictation. Click Enable. The same screen holds the shortcut, the microphone, and the languages you speak.

Leave Microphone source on Automatic unless you have a reason to change it. Automatic is the default in Apple's settings. If you use a headset or a USB microphone, pick it here so Dictation listens to the right input. Voice Control is different. Apple says Voice Control replaces standard Dictation when it is turned on, so turn it off if you want standard Dictation.

Most people do not need a special microphone. In one vendor sample of 507 users, 331 of them (65%) dictated through a built-in laptop or desktop microphone. The sample is small and opt-in, so use it as a rough sign, not a rule.

blocks.text: Dictate an email in Apple Mail, step by step

The steps below use the menu names from Apple's current Dictation help. That page defaults to macOS 27 and lists macOS Tahoe 26 as an earlier version. Menus can shift a little between releases. If a name on your Mac looks different, search the Edit menu for Dictation, then follow the same order.
Say punctuation and new lines out loud

In supported languages, Dictation inserts commas, periods, and question marks for you. You can turn that off under Dictation in Keyboard settings. When you want a specific mark, say its name, such as “exclamation mark”.

Line breaks are the part most people miss. Say “new line” for one Return. Say “new paragraph” for two Returns, which gives you a blank line between paragraphs. A short email usually needs a new paragraph after the greeting and another before the sign off.
Few people rely on these commands yet. In one vendor report, 91 of 269 users (34%) had ever used a spoken punctuation command. Test them in a draft before you rely on them for a client email.

blocks.title: Sign off cleanly
blocks.text: Say “new paragraph” before your sign off, so your name starts on its own line. Check the spacing once in the draft.
Stop dictation, and what happens when you pause
Press Escape to stop. You can also press the Microphone key, if your keyboard has one, or the Dictation shortcut. Dictation also stops on its own after 30 seconds with no detected speech.

The 30 second rule catches people who pause to think. If you stop to read a note, Dictation may end before you speak again. Click where you want to continue, then choose Edit > Start Dictation. Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout, so the pause timer is the thing to watch.
Proofread dictated text with Writing Tools
Dictation can mishear names, addresses, and numbers, so read every line before you send. If Apple Intelligence is available on your Mac, Writing Tools can help you tighten the wording.

To open it, select the text, Control-click it, choose Writing Tools, then Show Writing Tools. The options include Rewrite with Friendly, Professional, or Concise, Proofread, and Summarize or Key Points. Click Done when you are finished.

Apple's Writing Tools page uses Notes as its example and does not name Mail. Check that the menu appears on your Mac before you plan around it. If it does not appear, read the email aloud once before you send.
Dictate in iCloud.com Mail in a browser

If you use Mail in a browser at iCloud.com, the steps change. Go to icloud.com/mail, sign in, and click Compose in the top-right corner. From elsewhere on iCloud.com, use Create New in the toolbar, then Email Message.

Apple's iCloud page does not mention dictation. System Dictation may work in a browser text field, but that is an inference from how Dictation works, not a documented step. Test it with one short line before you rely on it.
How long dictated emails run, and what the numbers say

Email dictations tend to be short. In a Voibe report built on August 2026 data, email dictations averaged 17.1 words each. AI assistant apps averaged 38.6 words per dictation. The full sample holds 89,791 dictations from 507 opt-in users.

The same sample reports a median dictation speed of 122 words per minute, against a commonly cited typing average of 40 wpm. Speed is not the goal in email. Accuracy is. Treat these numbers as one vendor's sample, not a survey of Mail users.
Which Macs get the newest dictation model

Dictation itself ships with macOS. The newer on-device model that improves spelling, punctuation, and capitalization is narrower. Apple lists it as an Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27, for English, on Mac models with an M3 or later chip and at least 12 GB of unified memory.

If your Mac does not meet those needs, the steps in this guide do not change. The improved spelling and capitalization may not apply to you, though. Check your chip and memory before you expect those results.
Mistakes people make when dictating email

items: Starting Dictation before clicking in the body. Click into the message body first, or Dictation has no cursor to write into.
Looking for a Dictation button in the toolbar. Apple's Mail guide has no dictation section, so use the Edit menu.
Letting the 30 second timer end a thought. Keep talking, or click back in and choose Edit > Start Dictation.
Trusting names and addresses. Check every recipient in the To and Cc lines before you send.
Forgetting the sign off. Say “new paragraph” before your name so the signature starts on its own line.
Skipping the Subject line. Click the Subject field, dictate a short line, and read it once.

blocks.text: When Start Dictation is missing or stops working

Start with the Edit menu. Click inside the message body, then open Edit again. In the 2022 community thread, the microphone icon appeared only after that click. If the item is still missing, check that Dictation is enabled in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation.

Next, look at Voice Control. Apple says it replaces standard Dictation when it is on. Turn it off, then test Dictation again in the body of a blank draft. Keep the test short, so you know quickly whether the fix worked.

Some online fixes, such as privacy settings or Screen Time limits, are not covered by the Apple pages this guide relies on. Try the steps above first, and change one setting at a time, so you can tell which change helped.

blocks.title: Menu names can differ
blocks.text: The Mail menu path has not been confirmed against every macOS release. Apple's Dictation pages default to macOS 27 and list Tahoe 26 as an earlier version. If a name differs on your Mac, search the Edit menu for Dictation.
Next steps after your first dictated email

Once you can dictate a message, attachments are the next thing most people need. The guide on [how to add an attachment in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/add-an-attachment-to-an-email-in-apple-mail) covers photos and large files.

If you sign off the same way every day, build a signature so you do not dictate it again. See [how to create an email signature in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-apple-mail). To hold a dictated message until a set time, read [how to schedule an email to send later in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-apple-mail).
Curious whether speaking is faster than typing for you? Try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) and compare your numbers.

faq.question: Does Apple Mail have its own dictation button?
faq.answer: No. Apple Mail has no dedicated dictation feature, and Apple's Mail User Guide has no section on voice input. You use macOS Dictation, started from Edit > Start Dictation with the cursor in the message body, or from the Dictation shortcut.

faq.question: Why is Start Dictation missing from the Edit menu?
faq.answer: Click inside the message body first, then check the Edit menu again. If it is still missing, make sure Dictation is on in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation. Turn Voice Control off too, because it replaces standard Dictation.

faq.question: What shortcut starts Dictation on a Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's current dictation page does not name a default. Apple's older help for macOS 10.15 says the default is to press Fn twice. Check the Shortcut pop-up in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation on your own Mac.

faq.question: How long can I keep dictating in one go?
faq.answer: Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. Dictation stops by itself after 30 seconds with no detected speech, so keep talking or restart it from Edit > Start Dictation.

faq.question: Can I dictate in a language other than English?
faq.answer: Yes, if the language is in your Dictation list. Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and check Languages. Automatic punctuation applies only in supported languages, and the improved on-device model is English only.

faq.question: Which Macs get the improved dictation model?
faq.answer: Apple lists it as an Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27. It works in English on Mac models with an M3 or later chip and at least 12 GB of unified memory.

faq.question: Can I dictate in iCloud.com Mail?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud Mail page does not mention dictation. System Dictation may work in a browser text field, but Apple does not document that, so test it with one line first.

faq.question: Will Writing Tools fix my dictated email?
faq.answer: It can proofread and rewrite text when Apple Intelligence is available on your Mac. Select the text, Control-click it, choose Writing Tools, then Show Writing Tools. It does not replace your own read-through before you send.

steps.name: Turn on Dictation
steps.text: Open the Apple menu and choose System Settings. Click Keyboard, then Dictation. Click Enable if Dictation is off.
steps.tip: Leave Microphone source on Automatic unless you use a headset or USB microphone.

steps.name: Check your shortcut
steps.text: In the same Dictation panel, open the Shortcut pop-up menu. Choose Customize if you want to record your own keys.
steps.tip: Apple's current page does not name a default. An older Apple page for macOS 10.15 says Fn pressed twice.

steps.name: Start a new message
steps.text: Open Apple Mail and start a new message from the File menu. You can dictate the body before you fill in the recipients.
steps.tip: Writing the body first keeps you from sending before the text is ready.

steps.name: Click into the message body
steps.text: Click in the body of the message, below the To, Cc, and Subject lines. Dictation writes at the cursor, so the cursor must be in the body.
steps.tip: In the 2022 community thread, the microphone icon appeared only after this click.

steps.name: Start Dictation from the Edit menu
steps.text: With the cursor in the body, choose Edit > Start Dictation. Dictation starts listening. Speak at a normal pace.
steps.tip: You can also press the Microphone key, if your keyboard has one, or the Dictation shortcut you set.

steps.name: Dictate the greeting and body
steps.text: Say the greeting, then the body. Say “new line” for one Return and “new paragraph” for a blank line. Speak the email in the order you want it to read.
steps.tip: Pause between sentences. A pause shorter than 30 seconds keeps Dictation running.

steps.name: Say punctuation when you need it
steps.text: Dictation adds commas, periods, and question marks in supported languages. Say “exclamation mark” or another punctuation name when you want a specific mark.
steps.tip: Scan the punctuation after you finish, especially the question marks.

steps.name: Stop Dictation
steps.text: Press Escape to stop. You can also press the Microphone key or the Dictation shortcut. If you go quiet for 30 seconds, Dictation stops on its own.
steps.tip: To continue later, click where you want to resume, then choose Edit > Start Dictation again.

steps.name: Fill in the recipients and Subject
steps.text: Click the To field and type the address, or dictate it. Check each name and address, because dictation can mishear them. Then click the Subject field.
steps.tip: Choose Edit > Start Dictation again in the Subject field if you want to speak a short line.

steps.name: Proofread with Writing Tools
steps.text: Select the text you want to check. Control-click it, choose Writing Tools, then Show Writing Tools, and pick Proofread or Rewrite.
steps.tip: Writing Tools needs Apple Intelligence. If the menu is missing on your Mac, read the email aloud instead.

steps.name: Finish and send
steps.text: Click Done when Writing Tools is finished. Read the whole email once more, then click Send in the Mail toolbar.
steps.tip: A final read catches names, addresses, and numbers that dictation may have heard wrong.

shortcuts.action: Older default on macOS 10.15, check yours

troubleshooting.problem: The Edit menu has no Start Dictation item
troubleshooting.fix: Click inside the message body, then open Edit again. In the 2022 community thread, that click was the fix. If it is still missing, check that Dictation is enabled under System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation.

troubleshooting.problem: Dictation starts but the words do not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Microphone source pop-up in Dictation settings. It defaults to Automatic, so choose your headset or USB microphone if Automatic picked the wrong input. Then test in a blank draft.

troubleshooting.problem: Dictation stops in the middle of an email
troubleshooting.fix: Dictation stops on its own after 30 seconds with no detected speech. Click back in the body where you stopped, choose Edit > Start Dictation, and keep going.

troubleshooting.problem: Writing Tools does not appear after Control-click
troubleshooting.fix: Writing Tools needs Apple Intelligence. Apple's page does not confirm that the option appears in Mail on every Mac, so read the email aloud before you send.
Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation > Shortcut and check the key combination. Choose Customize to record a new one. Older Apple help says the default is Fn pressed twice.
